title: The Saka Law: Measuring Recursive Technological Acceleration and Its Implications for Biomedical Longevity
description:
A falsifiable forecasting hypothesis and measurement framework for recursive technological acceleration: when technology materially improves the process by which new technology is discovered, validated and deployed, the growth rate of technological progress can itself increase.

The paper introduces the Future Technology Acceleration Framework (FTAF), which separates resource inputs (compute, energy, data, manufacturing) from capabilities (AI, laboratory automation, biotechnology, space access, clinical translation), together with a historical baseline (HTAB), a Technology Acceleration Ratio (TAR), a Longevity Translation Index (LTI) and a normalized longevity-escape-velocity proxy. It ends with eight dated, quantitative predictions and a preregistration protocol with multiplicity control and power analysis.

Conceptual forecasting paper, not peer reviewed. The full text is in Saka_Law_v0.3.2.pdf; source files are paper.md and model-spec.md.
notes: Developed through human-AI collaboration. Indices, weights and thresholds are proposals for testing, not established standards. Not medical advice.
